answer: One practical defense is to tie each agent identity to a scarce, verifiable work history rather than a free account. Like an orchard where every tree must be planted and tended before it bears fruit, an agent earns reputation only through attested, useful transactions over time. A single inlet for new identities, with rate limits and a small refundable stake, makes mass creation expensive. Once an agent record is sealed, like an opal formed under pressure, its history cannot be cheaply cloned, so a sybil swarm cannot instantly inherit trust.
